=== Web Results ===

Working on projects | uv - Astral Docs
  URL: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/
  # [Working on projects](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/#working-on-projects)
## [Creating a new project](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/#creating-a-new-project)
You can create a new Python project using the `uv init` command:

```
$ uv init hello-world
$ cd hello-world
```

```
$ mkdir hello-world
$ cd hello-world
$ uv init
```

```
$ uv run hello-world
Hello from hello-world!
```

## [Viewing your version](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/#viewing-your-version)
```
$ uv version
hello-world 0.7.0
```

## [Running commands](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/#running-commands)
```
$ uv run example.py
```

Creating projects | uv - Astral Docs
  URL: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/init/
  # [Creating projects](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/init/#creating-projects)
uv supports creating a project with `uv init`.

## [Libraries](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/init/#libraries)
```
$ uv init --lib example-lib
```

## [Creating a project without a build system](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/init/#creating-a-project-without-a-build-system)
```
$ uv init --no-package example-app
```

```
$ cd example-app
$ uv run main.py
Hello from example-app!
```

## [Creating a minimal project](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/init/#creating-a-minimal-project)
```
$ uv init example-bare --bare --description "Hello world" --author-from git --vcs git --pin-python
```

Using uv to build and install Python CLI apps - mathspp
  URL: https://mathspp.com/blog/using-uv-to-build-and-install-python-cli-apps
  This practical tutorial shows how to use uv to build and install custom Python CLI applications globally on your system.

content.text:
The uv documentation says to use `uv init`:

```
$ uv init hello-world
$ cd hello-world
```

You can also run `uv init` with no name inside an existing empty directory, and it creates the project there.

The docs list a few variants:
- `uv init --lib example-lib` creates a library.
- `uv init --no-package example-app` creates a project without a build system.
- `uv init example-bare --bare` creates a minimal project.

Sources: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/ and https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/init/
